guide.name: The Appalachian Trail from Springer Mountain to Katahdin
guide.description: The trail towns, outfitters, hostels and diners that keep Appalachian Trail hikers going from Georgia to Maine, in trail order, with stops worth a drive for anyone visiting.

properties.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
properties.notes: Where most northbound hikers start, with the stone arch, the hiker registration area and the long staircase beside a 729-foot waterfall. The approach trail to Springer adds about 8.5 miles; drivers can see the falls from the top or bottom parking areas.
properties.address: 166 Amicalola Falls State Park Rd, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Amicalola Falls Lodge
properties.notes: A state park lodge on the ridge above the falls with long views over the foothills and an on-site restaurant. An easy first or last night for hikers and their families.
properties.address: 418 Amicalola Falls Lodge Rd, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Springer Mountain
properties.notes: The southern terminus, marked by a bronze plaque and the first white blaze. A Forest Service road gets you within about a mile, so day visitors can walk up and back; check road conditions in winter.
properties.address: Forest Service Road 42, Chattahoochee National Forest, GA

match.skip: No matching Apple Maps listing near this point (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: Blood Mountain
properties.notes: The highest point on the Georgia AT, topped by a stone shelter built in the 1930s and wide views from the rock slabs. A seasonal bear canister rule applies to overnight hikers on this stretch; check the Forest Service site.
properties.address: Byron Reece Trailhead, US-129, Blairsville, GA 30512

properties.name: Mountain Crossings at Walasi-Yi
properties.notes: The outfitter in a 1930s stone building that the trail passes straight through, about 30 miles in. Famous for pack shakedowns, and for the tree out front hung with boots from hikers who quit here.

properties.name: Dicks Creek Gap
properties.notes: The road crossing hikers use to reach Hiawassee, about 11 miles west, for resupply and a motel night on Lake Chatuge. Hiker shuttles run in the spring season; drivers can park here for a walk toward the North Carolina line.

properties.name: Outdoor 76
properties.notes: An independent outfitter on Franklin's main street, known for careful shoe fitting, hiker services and a cold beer after a day outside. Hiker shuttles between the trail gaps and town run in the spring season.

properties.name: Lazy Hiker Brewing
properties.notes: A brewery in Franklin's old town hall and fire station, with a patio and food trucks. A good spot to celebrate crossing into North Carolina.

properties.name: Nantahala Outdoor Center
properties.notes: The trail drops straight into this river outfitter in the Nantahala Gorge, with a gear store, bunkhouse and River's End restaurant overlooking the rapids. Watch kayakers on the river, then face the long climb out to Cheoah Bald.

properties.name: Fontana Village Resort
properties.notes: A lakeside resort village of cabins, a lodge and a general store, the last real stop before the Smokies. Hikers often take a zero here before the climb into the park.

properties.name: Fontana Dam
properties.notes: The tallest dam in the eastern US, which the AT crosses on its way into Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The lakeside shelter just south of the dam is known to hikers as the Fontana Hilton.
properties.address: Fontana Dam Rd, Fontana Dam, NC 28733

properties.name: Kuwohi
properties.notes: The highest point on the entire AT, formerly Clingmans Dome, with a concrete ramp to an observation tower. The access road closes in winter; check the National Park Service site before driving up.

properties.name: Newfound Gap
properties.notes: The big overlook on the North Carolina and Tennessee line where the trail crosses the park's main road. Hikers hitch or shuttle down to Gatlinburg from here; drivers can walk a few miles north toward Charlies Bunion.

properties.name: Sugarlands Visitor Center
properties.notes: The park's main visitor center just outside Gatlinburg, for backcountry permits, ranger advice and exhibits. Thru-hikers need a Smokies permit before entering; check the park site for current rules.
properties.address: 1420 Fighting Creek Gap Rd, Gatlinburg, TN 37738

properties.name: Pancake Pantry
properties.notes: A Gatlinburg breakfast institution since 1960, with a long menu of pancakes and crepes. Expect a line on weekends; it moves.

properties.name: Max Patch
properties.notes: A grassy bald with 360-degree views, a couple of days south of Hot Springs. Camping and fires are banned on the summit and the access road is gravel; come at sunrise or on a weekday.
properties.address: Max Patch Rd, Hot Springs, NC 28743

properties.name: Bluff Mountain Outfitters
properties.notes: Hot Springs' longtime outfitter and resupply store, back in business at a new spot on Bridge Street after the 2024 floods. The AT runs right down the main street outside.

properties.name: Hot Springs Resort & Spa
properties.notes: Private outdoor tubs filled with natural mineral water beside Spring Creek, plus campsites and cabins. A soak here is the classic Hot Springs reward; book tubs ahead on weekends.

properties.name: Spring Creek Tavern
properties.notes: A tavern with a deck over Spring Creek, burgers, local beer and live music some nights. The town's main gathering place for hikers and paddlers.

properties.name: Smoky Mountain Diner
properties.notes: A small-town diner known for big breakfasts and plain home cooking. Closed some days, so check before you go.

properties.name: Steel Rails Coffee House
properties.notes: A coffee shop in downtown Erwin, the railroad town where the trail crosses the Nolichucky River. Erwin was hit hard by the 2024 floods; call hostels ahead and check the Unicoi County tourism site for what is open.

properties.name: Carvers Gap
properties.notes: The parking area at the start of the Roan Highlands balds, some of the finest open walking on the trail. Walk north over Round Bald and Jane Bald; it is often windy and cold, even in summer.
properties.address: TN-143 at NC-261, Roan Mountain, TN 37687

properties.name: Mountain Harbour Bed & Breakfast
properties.notes: A bed and breakfast near the trail below the Roan, known among hikers for a huge breakfast and shuttles to Carvers Gap. Its hostel was being rebuilt after Hurricane Helene; check the official site.

properties.name: Damascus Diner
properties.notes: A homestyle diner with hiker-size portions in the self-styled Trail Town USA. Good for breakfast before a walk on the Creeper Trail.

properties.name: Damascus Old Mill Inn
properties.notes: An inn in an old mill on a millpond at the edge of town, with a restaurant and pub on the water. The comfortable choice in a town full of hostels.

properties.name: Virginia Creeper Trail
properties.notes: A rail trail that shares the AT's route through downtown Damascus, with bike rentals and shuttles in town. The 17 miles west to Abingdon are open; the climb east toward Whitetop was damaged in the 2024 floods, so check the Visit Damascus site.

properties.name: Grayson Highlands State Park
properties.notes: High grassy balds and rock outcrops where wild ponies graze along the trail. Easy to reach by car for a short walk; please do not feed or pet the ponies.
properties.address: 829 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

properties.name: Angels Rest Hiker's Haven
properties.notes: A hostel on a wooded lot at the foot of Angels Rest, walking distance to the grocery and restaurants. Offers bunks, camping, shuttles and parking for section hikers.

properties.name: McAfee Knob Trailhead
properties.notes: Start of the climb to McAfee Knob, the ledge that is probably the most photographed spot on the AT. It is about 8 miles round trip; the lot fills early on weekends, so arrive at dawn or come midweek.

properties.name: Appalachian Trail Conservancy Visitor Center
properties.notes: The ATC's headquarters near the trail's midpoint, where thru-hikers have their photo taken for the yearly album. Stop in for maps, advice and to sign the register.

properties.name: Jefferson Rock
properties.notes: A balanced slab of shale on the AT above the meeting of the Potomac and Shenandoah. A short climb from Lower Town by stone steps.
properties.address: Jefferson Rock Trail, Harpers Ferry, WV 25425

properties.name: The Town's Inn
properties.notes: Two pre-Civil War stone houses on High Street in Lower Town, with simple private rooms and a casual restaurant, a few steps from the trail. A central base for exploring the national historical park.

properties.name: Appalachian Trail Museum
properties.notes: A small museum in an old grist mill near the trail's midpoint, with early hiker gear and a trail shelter built by Earl Shaffer, the first thru-hiker. Open seasonally; check the official site.

properties.name: The Doyle Hotel
properties.notes: A brick hotel and bar that has fed AT hikers since the trail was young, right on the route through town. Classic American food and cold beer.

properties.name: Presbyterian Church of the Mountain
properties.notes: The church opened a hiker center for thru-hikers in 1976 and calls it the oldest hostel on the trail. Arrangements change from year to year, so check with the church before counting on a bunk.
properties.address: Main St and Church Ln, Delaware Water Gap, PA 18327

properties.name: Village Farmer & Bakery
properties.notes: A farm market and bakery best known for its deep-dish fruit pies, with a hot dog and slice deal hikers love.
properties.address: 13 Broad St, Delaware Water Gap, PA 18327

properties.name: Deer Head Inn
properties.notes: A Victorian inn that has hosted live jazz for decades, a few steps from the trail. Good for an evening set and dinner.
properties.address: 5 Main St, Delaware Water Gap, PA 18327

properties.name: Mount Tammany
properties.notes: The cliff-top view straight down into the Delaware Water Gap, reached by a steep side trail from the AT's New Jersey trailhead. Busy on weekends; start early.
properties.address: Dunnfield Creek Trailhead, Old Mine Rd, Columbia, NJ 07832

properties.name: Bear Mountain State Park
properties.notes: The trail climbs Bear Mountain on rebuilt stone steps, then passes through the Trailside Museums and Zoo, its lowest point. The park inn and lakeside lawns make it an easy family day.
properties.address: Palisades Interstate Pkwy and US-9W, Bear Mountain, NY 10911

properties.name: Kent Falls State Park
properties.notes: A series of cascades with a short stair trail alongside, a few miles north of the village. A good stop for drivers following the trail through the Housatonic Valley.

properties.name: Fife 'n Drum Restaurant & Inn
properties.notes: A long-running restaurant, pub and small inn on Kent's main street, with live music some nights. Kent is about a mile from the trail; hikers often walk in for a meal.

properties.name: Inn at Long Trail
properties.notes: A rustic inn near where the AT and the Long Trail split, with McGrath's Irish Pub built around a boulder. A favorite night out for hikers and skiers alike.

properties.name: Lou's Restaurant & Bakery
properties.notes: Hanover's breakfast and lunch counter since 1947, with pastries and big plates. The trail runs right through the Dartmouth town on Main Street.

properties.name: Hanover Inn
properties.notes: A historic hotel on the Dartmouth Green, on the AT's path through town. The upscale option for visitors meeting a hiker.

properties.name: Pinkham Notch Visitor Center
properties.notes: The Appalachian Mountain Club's base below Mount Washington, with trail advice, a dining room and Joe Dodge Lodge. Check the higher-summits forecast here before heading into the Presidentials.

properties.name: Colonial Fort Inn
properties.notes: A small family-run motel on Gorham's main street, long known to hikers as Hikers Paradise. Plain rooms with private baths, in the resupply town between the Presidentials and the Mahoosucs.

properties.name: Shaw's Hiker Hostel
properties.notes: A Monson institution before the 100-Mile Wilderness, known for a big breakfast, food drops and its own gear shop. Book well ahead in late summer.

properties.name: Appalachian Trail Hostel & Outfitters
properties.notes: The northernmost hiker service on the trail, with lodging, an outfitter, shuttles and help with Baxter State Park rules for a Katahdin climb.

properties.name: Katahdin Stream Campground
properties.notes: The campground at the base of the Hunt Trail, the AT's final climb. Day-use parking and campsites must be reserved; check the Baxter State Park site for rules and the hiking season.
properties.address: Park Tote Rd, Baxter State Park, ME 04462

properties.name: Katahdin
properties.notes: The northern terminus at Baxter Peak, marked by the weathered wooden sign. It is a long, rocky, exposed day hike; the park closes trails in bad weather and outside its season.
